body:
## Pull request overview

This pull request refactors the AG Grid plugin to use field widgets from `@object-ui/fields` instead of hardcoded cell formatters, achieving consistency across the ObjectUI ecosystem and eliminating ~160 lines of duplicated formatting logic.

**Changes:**
- Introduces a unified rendering approach using field widgets for 21 field types (text, number, boolean, date, currency, email, phone, url, color, rating, image, avatar, etc.)
- Replaces switch-case formatter logic with reusable field widget components that support both read-only and edit modes
- Improves security by ensuring fallback renderers use DOM creation instead of HTML string concatenation

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-aggrid/src/field-renderers.tsx | New module implementing AG Grid custom renderers/editors using React field widgets with createRoot, including factory functions for field metadata injection |
| packages/plugin-aggrid/src/ObjectAgGridImpl.tsx | Refactored to use field widget renderers instead of hardcoded formatters; removed ~160 lines of switch-case logic and unused imports; fallback renderers now use safe DOM creation |
| packages/plugin-aggrid/package.json | Added `@object-ui/fields` workspace dependency |
| pnpm-lock.yaml | Updated lockfile with new dependency and platform-specific binary metadata |

<details>
<summary>Files not reviewed (1)</summary>

* **pnpm-lock.yaml**: Language not supported
</details>

The field type 'lookup' appears in both the `fieldWidgetTypes` array (line 437) and in the fallback switch statement (line 456). This creates redundant code where the lookup type will use the field widget renderer but the fallback case will never be reached. Remove the 'lookup' and 'master_detail' cases from the fallback switch statement since they're already handled by the field widget renderer.

The new `field-renderers.tsx` module introduces critical rendering and editing logic for AG Grid cells but lacks test coverage. Given that this package has existing test coverage (see `index.test.ts` and `object-aggrid.test.ts`), tests should be added for the new field renderer classes. Consider adding tests for: 1) Widget mapping in `getFieldWidget()`, 2) Renderer lifecycle (init, refresh, destroy), 3) Editor lifecycle and value handling, 4) Fallback behavior when widgets don't exist, and 5) Memory cleanup (root.unmount()).

The `getFieldWidget()` function recreates the `widgetMap` object on every call, which is inefficient. The widgetMap should be defined as a module-level constant outside the function to avoid unnecessary object allocations. This will improve performance, especially when rendering large grids with many cells.
```suggestion
const widgetMap: Record<string, React.ComponentType<any>> = {
  text: TextField,
  textarea: TextAreaField,
  number: NumberField,
  currency: CurrencyField,
  percent: PercentField,
  boolean: BooleanField,
  select: SelectField,
  date: DateField,
  datetime: DateTimeField,
  time: TimeField,
  email: EmailField,
  phone: PhoneField,
  url: UrlField,
  password: PasswordField,
  color: ColorField,
  rating: RatingField,
  image: ImageField,
  avatar: AvatarField,
  lookup: LookupField,
  slider: SliderField,
  code: CodeField,
};

function getFieldWidget(fieldType: string): React.ComponentType<any> | null {
```
Fixed in 97ae174. Removed the redundant 'lookup' case from the fallback switch since it's already handled by the field widget renderer in line 437.
Fixed in 97ae174. The refresh() method now updates textContent for the fallback case and returns true to avoid unnecessary DOM recreation.

Fixed in 97ae174. Added comprehensive test coverage with 17 new tests in field-renderers.test.tsx covering widget mapping, renderer/editor lifecycle, fallback behavior, and memory cleanup. All 29 tests now passing.
Fixed in 97ae174. Moved widgetMap to module level to avoid object recreation on every call, improving performance especially for large grids.
